title: Khajuraho and Orchha (Batch 5)
selection: Batch 5. Khajuraho (6 sections, two of them state filler) and Orchha (5, two filler). Adds who it's for, practical info, things to do, how to reach, shopping, food, common mistakes and FAQs, plus fuller overviews (pending review). Source conflicts noted: Khajuraho surviving temples 20 vs 25 (both on MP Tourism's page); Orchha founding 15th century (existing ORC1) vs early 16th century (Wikipedia, MP Tourism); cenotaphs 14 (Incredible India) vs 15 (MP Tourism); Laxmi Narayan temple 1622 vs 1662. khajuraho-orchha-gwalior-5-days is left for the audit.

places.name: Khajuraho
places.summary: The Chandela capital's temples — 20 of a legendary 85 survive, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.seoTitle: Khajuraho Travel Guide: Temples, Dance Festival & Panna
places.seoDescription: Plan Khajuraho: the UNESCO Chandela temples, Kandariya Mahadev, the Khajuraho Dance Festival (late Feb–Mar), the airport and Panna nearby.

overview.text:
Khajuraho, named after the khajura or date palm, was a capital of the Chandela kings, who built its temples around 950–1050 AD. Of a legendary 85 temples, a group survives as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, famous for Nagara-style spires and sculptures of deities, celestial women and daily life. The erotic carvings that made it famous are only about a tenth of the whole, and both Hindu and Jain temples stand here.

The Western group, beside the archaeological museum, holds the finest: Lakshmana, Kandariya Mahadev with more than 870 sculptures, Chitragupta and Vishwanatha. The Eastern group has the Jain temples, and the 9th-century Chausath Yogini is the oldest. The town has its own airport, Raneh and Pandav falls and Panna National Park are close, and the Khajuraho Dance Festival runs from late February into March.

places.name: Orchha
places.summary: A Bundela capital on the Betwa: palaces, the Ram Raja temple and riverside cenotaphs.
places.seoTitle: Orchha Travel Guide: Fort, Ram Raja & Cenotaphs
places.seoDescription: Plan Orchha: the fort's Raj Mahal and Jahangir Mahal, the Ram Raja Mandir, the Laxmi Narayan murals and the Betwa cenotaphs; fort hours.

overview.text:
Orchha, on the Betwa river, was founded by the Bundela chief Rudra Pratap Singh in the early 16th century, and its palaces, temples and cenotaphs still stand almost untouched. The fort complex holds the Raj Mahal, the Sheesh Mahal, now a heritage hotel, and the Jahangir Mahal, built to welcome the Mughal emperor and tiled in turquoise.

Orchha is the only place outside Ayodhya where Rama is worshipped as a king, at the Ram Raja Temple, whose evening aarti draws crowds. The Laxmi Narayan temple is covered in murals and has a climbable roof, and the Bundela cenotaphs line the river. Rafting on the Betwa and a riverside sanctuary add to a slow stay. Jhansi, about 17 km away, is the railhead.

how_to_reach.text:
By train: Jhansi Junction, about 17 km away, is the main railhead; Orchha's own station is about 6 km from the Ram Raja Temple.

By air: Gwalior airport is 142 km away.

By road: buses and taxis run from Jhansi.
